overview: This bill, called the New BANK Act, would require federal financial regulators to publish yearly reports on applications to start new banks and credit unions. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, which charters national banks, the National Credit Union Administration, the Federal Reserve and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) would each report how many applications they received, approved, denied or saw withdrawn, how long approvals took on average, and common reasons applications failed. A joint report would cover state-chartered banks and credit unions, broken out state by state. As of February 25, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say publishing these numbers would show whether the approval process is slow or discouraging new banks and credit unions, helping Congress and the public hold regulators accountable.
against: Critics say the bill only adds reporting requirements and does nothing directly to speed up approvals, while creating extra work for agencies and state regulators.
